newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat on post-election calm.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat on post-election calm.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates ended up 5 basis points at 19.80 percent as temporary liquidity pressures marginally outweighed market relief after Sunday's mid-term elections went ahead with little trouble, traders said.
"The market was under a bit of pressure from Banco de Mexico's cutoff date tomorrow, today is the last day for grabbing liquidity," a dealer said.
Banks have to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts they hold with the central bank on Wednesday.
"The election results were well received, and pre-election jitters we saw last week were dispelled," a fixed-income analyst said.

Mexicans voted on Sunday to renew the lower house of Congress, one-quarter of the Senate, several state governors and for the first time in modern Mexico, a mayor for the capital. The Presidency was not up for renewal.
The all-powerful Institutional Revolutionary Party also gracefully accepted preliminary returns that showed it had suffered its worst results since it was founded 1929.
Dealers said a strong peso also helped keep secondary market rates stable. Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 2.25 centavos firmer on the day at 7.8990/7.9025.
Banco de Mexico drained 4.648 billion pesos from the market during the session.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile gained 40 basis points to 20.00 percent.
Traders predicted primary interest rates would fall across the board at the weekly central bank primary auction, whose results were expected at 1830 local time/2330 GMT.
A Reuters survey of nine money market traders, taken shortly before the central bank closed bids, showed they predicted an average placement rate of 18.56 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes.
This would be a fall of 139 basis points from last week's auction.
Dealers said they would keep a close eye on June inflation data, expected sometime on Wednesday.
Liquidity of 707 million pesos was due to return to the market on Wednesday from prior central bank operations.
